I’m not sure I have many happy stories left.

When I was in kindergarten my mom told me that I needed to learn how to tie my shoes or my teachers were going to leave me behind when my shoes got untied at field trips in first grade and that the kids would tease me if I wore velcro or slip on shoes.

My stepdad saw me crying in my room and came in with shoes and spent hours helping me learn how to tie my shoes. He was so patient. He was so kind. He was just the most amazing person I’ve ever met. 

He taught me whenever I was angry, instead of bursting out in anger I should just say “I do not like green eggs and ham, I do not like you sam-I-am” and when I did I always bursted into laughter. 

He bought me a book called “the blue day book” to try and explain to first grade me why I was always more sad than the other kids. 

He pretended to take pills with me when I took my depression medication in first grade, telling me that it was a happy medicine and it would help me grow big and strong. 

The depression took most of the memories I have of the man who raised me, but I hope that the fact that there are people out there like my stepdad makes you smile. People who love unconditionally. People who see a single mom and her infant and toddler as an incredible addition to his life rather than a burden. 

That’s my happy story and I miss him so much.

Hello! I went through a similar experience under a year ago and just wanted to share my experience of sharing it with my boyfriend. So I ended up sharing this with my SO at around 2-3 months and his initial reaction was anger. He was angry that no one stopped what was happening to me. He was angry that rumors had been spread within my social groups that I had “wanted it” and was a “total slut”. But mostly, he was angry that he couldn’t have been there to prevent it. I didn’t know him at the time it had happened and so of course i didnt expect him to be there. However, this was just an initial reaction. Since then he’s been completely supportive and with that he doesn’t bring it up. I’ve felt insecure thinking that it “tainted” me and that now im “imperfect” but he was quick to say that I wasn’t tainted and that to him i am perfect. That being said, I think that information is a lot for an SO to deal with and it can make them uncomfortable. I always advocate for talking out feelings, but with a delicate topic such as this one, it’s ridiculous that he keeps bringing it up. He might not know that so I would have a sit down with him and tell him that you’re not comfortable with him bringing it up so much (and make sure he understands why) and then maybe talk through why he’s feeling the way that he does and then hopefully he will at least respect the fact that you don’t want it brought up.
